chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muhammad ibn Umar al-Sabati who said:

I asked Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and divorced her before consummating the marriage. He said: 'There is no waiting period (iddah) upon her.' And I asked him about a woman whose husband died before consummating the marriage. He said: 'There is no waiting period upon her. The two cases are equal.'
ai.seo_question: What is the iddah (waiting period) for a wife if her husband dies or divorces her before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the waiting period (iddah) is not obligatory for a wife in cases of divorce or death before consummation (dakhul), establishing their legal equality in this specific matter. This ruling contrasts with the general iddah of four months and ten days prescribed for widowhood after consummation, highlighting the significance of physical union in establishing full marital rights and obligations in Shia jurisprudence. The narration serves as a key textual evidence for the principle that the bond of marriage is fully actualized only upon consummation, thereby simplifying the transition for the wife in these pre-consummation scenarios.
